story_type: helicopter bucket drops on a wildfire at the edge of a city
hook: The fire reached the houses. This helicopter emptied its bucket on it.
narration: This Marine helicopter dumped its whole bucket straight onto the flames.
In May 2014, the Cocos Fire hit San Marcos, California.
Santa Ana winds and drought pushed it right up to the neighborhoods.
The fires that week forced tens of thousands of people to evacuate across San Diego County.
Their buckets fill from lakes and ponds, then a valve in the bottom opens over the fire.
The biggest Marine helicopter carries a nine hundred gallon bucket.
[short pause] Over four days, Marine crews dropped more than five hundred forty thousand gallons of water across the county.
outcome: The Cocos Fire burned 1,995 acres and was fully contained eight days later.
title: Wildfire at the edge of San Marcos
description:
Marine Corps helicopters drop water on the Cocos Fire above San Marcos, California, on May 15, 2014, as the fire burns close to homes. The fire was fully contained on May 22 after burning 1,995 acres.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Pfc. Maxwell Pennington, Marine Corps Air Station Miramar, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/337222/3rd-maw-marines-fight-san-diego-county-wildfires
